claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Forming a core-shell structure with a low-density core and a high-strength shell is the proposed intervention.
A low-density core would reduce the overall density relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
A high-strength shell would maintain the material's strength at room temperature.
A high-strength shell would maintain the material's strength at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The core-shell material would have reduced density without a significant loss of mechanical properties relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The predicted retention of mechanical properties applies from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposal is restricted to mechanical stresses within the material's strength limits.
The magnitude of density reduction and property retention depends on the core and shell materials, their proportions, and the fabrication method.
A density reduction of less than 5% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr would reject the hypothesis.
A reduction of more than 10% in strength or toughness at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr would reject the hypothesis.
